title: Multiply Two Linked List Numbers
description:
You are given two non-empty singly linked lists `l1` and `l2` representing two non-negative integers in **most-significant-digit-first** order. Each node contains a single decimal digit (`0` through `9`), and neither number contains leading zeros except the number `0` itself.

Multiply the two integers and return their product as a singly linked list in most-significant-digit-first order (with no leading zeros except a single `0` if the product is zero). Because the numbers can have up to 200 digits, they may exceed 64-bit integer limits.
constraints: The number of nodes in each list is in the range [1, 200].
Neither input has leading zeros unless it is the single digit 0.
hints: Reverse both linked lists (or extract their digits in least-significant-digit-first order) so position `i` in `l1` times position `j` in `l2` contributes directly to output digit `i + j`.
Accumulate all partial products into an array of size `n + m`, propagate carries from least significant to most significant, strip leading zeros, and build the resulting linked list.
